title: A minor pentatonic in one position
summary: Follow the five-note pattern across all six strings at frets 5–8.
goal: Play the A minor pentatonic position up to C5 and return to A2 without rushing string changes.
body:
Before starting: practice C major across the strings and move comfortably between individual notes. Tune to Standard, A4 = 440 Hz.

A minor pentatonic uses five pitch names: A, C, D, E, G. They repeat in higher octaves. This position begins on A2 at string 6 fret 5 and reaches C5 at string 1 fret 8. Its highest note is C5, not the next A.

Keep the hand near fret 5. Suggested fingers are index at fret 5, ring at fret 7 and little finger at fret 8. Choose comfortable movement and release unnecessary pressure. The positions are a map to learn; the app measures audible pitch and attacks, not which finger followed that map.

Start at 50 BPM, with one quarter note per click. The ascent takes bars 1–3; bars 4–6 return to A2 and end with a rest. Practice one or two bars first if needed. When the full path feels comfortable, try 60 BPM; a new tempo creates different comparison conditions. Keep just one note sounding at a time so the result can give useful pitch evidence.

low-strings.title: 1. Begin with A2, C3, D3, E3
low-strings.body: Bar 1: string 6 frets 5, 8; string 5 frets 5, 7. Notice that each string begins at fret 5.

middle-strings.title: 2. Cross the middle strings
middle-strings.body: Bar 2: string 4 frets 5, 7 gives G3, A3; string 3 frets 5, 7 gives C4, D4.

high-strings.title: 3. Reach the top of the position
high-strings.body: Bar 3: string 2 frets 5, 8 gives E4, G4; string 1 frets 5, 8 gives A4, C5.

return-high.title: 4. Turn around without repeating C5
return-high.body: Bar 4 descends through A4, G4, E4, D4. Read each string change in tablature before playing.

return-home.title: 5. Return to A2 and leave space
return-home.body: Bars 5–6 continue C4, A3, G3, E3, D3, C3, A2, then a quarter rest. Review a recommended fragment after the attempt instead of automatically increasing the tempo.
